note: The English epigraphs are loose modern paraphrases cited by chapter only (“from Psalm 122”); the Swahili keeps that shape (“— kutoka Zaburi 122”). Each is rendered in the Swahili Union Version (SUV) tradition the shipped sw corpus quotes. Where a shipped *.sw.json already carries the SUV words they were pasted verbatim and the row is `mined` with that file; otherwise the row is `self_rendered` in SUV register (from memory of the SUV, no reachable PD text) and needs a native check.

Self-rendered choices worth a reviewer's eye: Psalm 91:2 uses SUV “Nitasema, Bwana ndiye kimbilio langu” (the-god-of-all-comfort.sw has a freer “Nitamwambia Bwana, ‘Ndiwe kimbilio langu…’”); Psalm 32:7 keeps SUV “sitara yangu” in the epigraph while the chapter body says the plainer “mahali pa kujificha” (hiding place) a child will follow; Enoch in chapter 7 is “Henoko … alikwenda pamoja na Mungu” (Genesis 5:24).

Terms: Jewish people = Wayahudi; Nazis = Wanazi; the hiding place “the Angels’ Crib” = “Kitanda cha Malaika”; the wall sign “Jesus is Victor” = “Yesu ni Mshindi”; the cat is SUV “Maher-shalal-hash-bazi” (Isaiah 8:1); “people with learning disabilities” = “watu wenye ulemavu wa akili”; series name follows series.json (“Taswira za Ujasiri”). No clock times needed conversion. AI-translated in-session; awaiting native review.
